title: AI NPCs make my game feel more alive
author: SneakerHunterDev
selftext:
I’ve been working on AI-driven NPCs that can perceive the world and even form alliances with you and protect you.

It completely changed how the world feels.

Small demo launches on Steam in 3 days!

Steam Page: https://theflairgame.com/on-steam?utm\_source=reddit&utm\_medium=social&utm\_campaign=snoopai

A Wishlist would really help me <3 

Have a nice day!

replies.author: CosmonautFrog
replies.body:
So imagine ChatGPT or whatever AI API you are using starts to charge x5 the amount (to avoid the astronomical debt they have), is that worth it? Also the +10 seconds time per response is completely crazy, it's 0% immersive.

And how do you manage that a player isn't spamming requests as crazy? That will make you broke easy in 10 seconds.

And how do you manage the API key exposal in game files? Do you have some intermediate API to hide the AI key?

IMHO not worth it. It's a really bad idea.

replies.author: SneakerHunterDev
replies.body:
the Costs are Low. I Can definitely cover them even if the prices rise (what I doubt). 
The Players cannot Spam requests as there are certain Interval Limits Set. 
The api key is not in the Client Game files (only on the server). 
But you are Right in terms of the Delay for the response. Gotta work on that

replies.author: CosmonautFrog
replies.body:
Even with intervals, if someone hit the allowed rate continuously will make you broke really fast. You're basically exposing a button to the client to expend your money.

If you increase the interval, then the feature will not contribute to the game at all.

Honestly not a good idea if it's not a local model.

comments.author: NotDennis2
comments.body: The issue that comes with this, is that for it to make sense, you need to make sure the NPC responds in a way the NPC would, which requires not replying normally to the endless things a player may say. So you need to limit it. At that point, it's cheapee (and makes more sense) to just do traditional game dialogue without AI.

replies.author: SneakerHunterDev
replies.body: I already adjust the responses according to the world and the npc!

replies.author: TheElsobky
replies.body: I disagree the whole point of AI is that you can give it lore books and knowledge books so they have only a specific set of knowledge to roleplay with. character ai for example has really strong rp capabilities. tbf its something I haven't seen done in games but still super cool.

replies.author: NotDennis2
replies.body: It would be cool if the nature of this technology didn't make it impossible for the NPCs to stay within the boundaries of what makes sense. It is the same technology flaw that lets Twitter users generate inappropriate pictures of minors. If you are going to limit such an AI to only respond to exactly what questions make sense, and have it respond "I don't know what you mean" to everything else, it is not viable to use generative AI for dialogue. It would be far too expensive for very little return.

replies.author: TheElsobky
replies.body: The whole point is that it’s a store of knowledge you give it and it dynamically answers, which you can’t do with traditional dialogue trees. And you can dynamically update the knowledge store. Costs money but increases immersion. Safeguards are only getting stronger. And for the trolls who try breaking it aren’t the target audience.

replies.author: NotDennis2
replies.body: You don't need to be a troll to break the AI, and I have to disagree, and argue that it is more likely to break immersion than to enhance it. You won't be able to generate NPC behaviour, just dialogue, and if it needs to be very specific knowledge, based on which character you're talking to, it will always make more sense to use prewritten dialogue.

replies.author: TheElsobky
replies.body:
not true. you can create or tie existing actions to the AI so it can trigger them based off the dialogue (ex; aggro state when user antagonizes an npc). now ofc I understand you'd have to program these manually. You can make the point that since you have access to what players are doing/saying to npcs you can create actions curated to that.   
  
But who knows in the future you may just be able to create very simple building blocks and the AI can improvise off of it (this is a stretch I know, but the 1st point still stands)

replies.author: NotDennis2
replies.body: If you are using generative AI to interpret player specific dialogue into predetermined states such as aggro, then it would be a silly decision to spend money on accessing such technology only for it to result in something you could quicker, cheaper and more reliably implement using dialogue options for the player to use.
